questions.domain: Inflation, Interest Rates, and the Economy
questions.prompt: A town has 50,000 people in the labor force; 2,000 are jobless and looking for work. What is the unemployment rate?
questions.intro: The labor force is people working or looking for work. Unemployment rate = unemployed ÷ labor force × 100.
sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (Unemployment): The unemployment rate is the share of the labor force that is jobless and looking for work. (https://www.bls.gov/cps/)

Federal Reserve (Monetary policy): The Federal Reserve sets a target range for the federal funds rate to pursue maximum employment and stable prices; it has a longer-run inflation goal of 2%. (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy.htm)

questions.domain: Inflation, Interest Rates, and the Economy

choices.text: A single bad month on the stock market
A rise in prices across the economy
A significant, widespread decline in economic activity

questions.correct_answer: A significant, widespread decline in economic activity
questions.intro: In a recession, output and spending fall, layoffs rise, and many businesses earn less. Recessions are part of the business cycle of expansions and contractions.
questions.feedback: A recession is a broad economic decline.

questions.prompt: Gas prices jump because supply is cut while demand stays the same. What explains the higher price?

choices.text: More supply with the same demand
Less supply with the same demand
Less demand with the same supply
Prices are set by law each day

questions.correct_answer: Less supply with the same demand
questions.intro: Prices respond to supply and demand: less supply or more demand pushes prices up.
questions.feedback: Reduced supply with steady demand raises prices.

questions.domain: Inflation, Interest Rates, and the Economy
questions.prompt: During a downturn, Rosa's stock index fund drops 20%. She has 30 years until retirement. What does history suggest?

choices.text: Staying invested has usually recovered over time
Stocks never recover after a drop
She should move everything to cash at once
She must sell her shares immediately by federal law

questions.correct_answer: Staying invested has usually recovered over time
questions.feedback: Long-term investors have historically recovered from downturns, though past results do not guarantee future ones.
